title: Opposing functions of gut immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T therapy.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (subscription-only, isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, no database cross-references, no text-mined accessions, no PMCID so no supplementary listing); scripts/paper_context.py found zero accessions and zero repository hits; ENA portal study search, Zenodo (0 hits) and Dryad (0 hits) searches found no deposit; the publisher full-text page returned HTTP 403 so the data availability statement could not be read; the one 2026 NCBI BioProject for CAR-T plus metagenome (PRJEB123871) belongs to a different 30-patient study, not this one.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the actual contents: 129 patients across three German centers, shotgun metagenomics (sequencing of all DNA in stool) plus targeted mass spectrometry of short-chain fatty acids and indole metabolites, and the progression/outcome associations. All of this comes from the abstract alone; I opened no data file.

a1_downloadable.note: No data found anywhere: paper is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC lists no supplementary files and no repository cross-references, and ENA, Zenodo and Dryad searches returned nothing. Human stool metagenomes from German clinical centers are typically controlled-access (European Genome-phenome Archive) when deposited at all. The publisher page is 403 so even the data availability statement is unreadable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label would be a clinical endpoint (disease progression / progression-free survival) held in hospital records for each patient; it is not visible in any public table and would have to be joined to metabolite and metagenome measurements that are themselves unavailable.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs (metabolite concentrations, species abundance tables) are not obtainable; raw sequencing reads would be excluded by policy even if a deposit existed.

a4_units_stated.note: Mass-spectrometry metabolite units (for example micromolar or nanograms per gram of stool) are presumably stated in the paywalled methods, but could not be verified in any file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The unit of analysis is the patient: 129 patients, well under the ~400 needed even for a pure classification task, and the outcome groups (progressors versus responders) would each be a few dozen people. This is the same failure as the scCT-DB candidate: many measurements, few independent subjects.

a6_fits_laptop.note: A 129-row metabolite plus species-abundance table would be tiny (well under 100 MB); only raw metagenomic reads would be large, and they are not needed. Size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no file exists to count rows in, so the paper's 129-patient claim cannot be cross-checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Clinical progression is a real measured outcome, not another model's output, and it is independent of the metabolite features. This killer would pass if the data existed.

existing_models.name: Microbiome-based machine-learning models for CAR-T response (Boruta-selected species classifiers, BioProject PRJEB123871 study)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as 'strong predictive performance' on 30 patients with B-cell lymphoma; split not verified by me and I did not retrieve the full paper.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not verified — only the BioProject abstract was retrieved.

integration.partner_dataset: none usable without the primary data
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not writable: with no accessible measurements there is nothing to join.

controls.positive_control: Would have been recovering the published valeric-acid association with progression, but this needs the unavailable data.
controls.external_validation: Other CAR-T microbiome cohorts exist (for example the 30-patient shotgun metagenomics study under BioProject PRJEB123871), but they cannot validate a model that cannot be trained.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the measurements underlying this paper are not publicly downloadable, and with 129 patients any model would describe three German centers' patients rather than CAR-T recipients generally.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gut bacterial metabolite levels measured before treatment to predict whether a cancer patient's disease progresses after CAR-T therapy.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-patient pre-treatment stool measurements: concentrations of short-chain fatty acids such as valeric acid and indole metabolites, plus bacterial species abundances from shotgun metagenomics. The paper reports 129 patients; I verified no count in any file.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no or time-to-event outcome for disease progression after CAR-T (engineered immune cell) therapy, taken from clinical follow-up records at the three treating centers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Hematology teams would use it to decide whether to delay therapy, avoid antibiotics or supplement a metabolite before infusion; even a failed model would show how little pre-treatment stool chemistry predicts relapse.

ml_idea: Predict post-CAR-T disease progression from pre-infusion stool metabolite concentrations and bacterial species abundances, with leave-one-center-out splits across the three German sites. Not executable: the data is not public and 129 patients is too few.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because no data file was located; a 129-row table would be trivial to handle on a laptop if it ever became available.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the independent patients with both a metabolite measurement and a recorded outcome. 129 total patients already kills it, before the separate question of whether any table can be downloaded.

verdict_reason: Data not public (paywalled, no supplement, no accession found) and only 129 patients, so A1 and A5 both fail.
